scenarios.description: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. The gold action item owner is that absent participant.

A task is assigned early in the meeting and later in the same meeting is either reassigned to someone else (status reassigned, owner = new owner, previous_owners lists the original) or dropped entirely (status dropped).

argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0201d: meeting "d" (detailed design) of series SY0201.

PROJECT
The team is designing a wearable step counter for seniors.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Helen  present
B  Marketing Expert (ME)  Tom  ABSENT, never speaks
C  User Interface designer (UI)  Priya  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Marcus  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0201a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, introduced the team and presented the project: a wearable step counter for seniors aged about sixty-five and up, which should be original, trendy and above all easy to use. She explained that the work will run in three stages (functional, conceptual and detailed design), and the team practised using the whiteboard. She gave the financial targets: a selling price of 30 euros, a maximum production cost of 12.50 euros per unit, and a profit target of 5 million euros from international sales. The team agreed that the device needs a large, high-contrast display and only one or two buttons. They discussed whether it should be a clip-on or a wristband and deferred that choice to the next meeting. A fall detection feature was proposed but parked as probably out of budget. The project manager then assigned individual work for the next meeting, which is in thirty minutes.
  decisions: The device will have a large, high-contrast display. The device will have minimal buttons, one or two at most. The choice between a clip-on and a wristband is deferred to the next meeting. Fall detection is parked for now because of the budget.
  actions: The marketing expert will research competitor step counters for seniors. The user interface designer had offered to do this, but the marketing expert took it on as market research. The marketing expert will prepare the user requirements. The industrial designer will prepare the working design, including components and battery life, and will compare rechargeable and replaceable batteries. The user interface designer will prepare the technical functions design. Each team member will present a few slides on their part at the next meeting. The project manager will write up the minutes and send them round. The cost of hypoallergenic silicone straps was raised as something someone should check, but nobody took it on.
  problems: It is not yet decided whether the device will be a clip-on (more accurate for steps) or a wristband (harder to lose, easier to remember). The 12.50 euro production cost limit is tight for a good screen and rules out fall detection for now. Nobody owns checking the cost of hypoallergenic silicone straps. There is no branding guidance in the brief yet.
  action item SY0201a.ai1: Research competitor step counters currently on the market for seniors, including their screens. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0201a.ai2: Check the cost of soft hypoallergenic silicone wrist straps. (owner no owner, active)
  action item SY0201a.ai3: Prepare the working design (internal workings and components), including battery life and rechargeable versus replaceable battery options, and present it at the next meeting. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0201a.ai4: Prepare the technical functions design (what the device has to do for the user) and present it at the next meeting. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0201a.ai5: Prepare the user requirements and present them at the next meeting. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0201a.ai6: Write up the minutes of the kickoff meeting and send them to the team. (owner A, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer proposed a clip-on device worn on the belt or pocket, because the hip is more accurate for step counting.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert proposed a wristband because it is visible and users remember to wear it.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed fall detection with alerts. It was parked as probably out of budget.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a replaceable watch-style battery. The industrial designer said he would look at both options, so it was not agreed.

[SY0201b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting and noted that the marketing expert was absent through illness, so his user requirements and competitor research could not be presented. She confirmed that the kickoff minutes had been sent round. The industrial designer presented the working design. He reported that a three-axis accelerometer makes a wristband accurate enough for step counting, and that a replaceable coin cell with a segment display would last about a year. A rechargeable battery would add about 1.50 euros and need regular charging. The user interface designer presented the technical functions. She proposed that the device show today's steps by default, with a single button that cycles to yesterday's steps and distance, and with setup done by holding the button down. The team chose a wristband, a replaceable coin cell battery, a high-contrast segment display and a single button. An hourly vibration reminder was left open because of its battery cost, and fall detection stayed parked. The task of checking strap costs was first given to the user interface designer and later moved to the industrial designer. Tasks for the absent marketing expert will be passed on to him by email.
  decisions: The device will be a wristband rather than a clip-on. The device will use a replaceable coin cell battery rather than a rechargeable one. The device will use a large, high-contrast segment display rather than a colour screen. The device will have a single button. By default it shows today's steps, and pressing the button cycles to yesterday's steps and then distance. Fall detection remains parked because of the budget.
  actions: The industrial designer will check the cost of soft hypoallergenic silicone wrist straps. This task was first given to the user interface designer. The user interface designer will prepare mock-ups of the interface, showing the display layout and the button behaviour, for the conceptual design meeting. The industrial designer will price the components, in particular the display and the case. The project manager will email the marketing expert today with the decisions and his tasks. The marketing expert will finish the competitor research, including screens, and send it round before the next meeting. The marketing expert will send his user requirements before the next meeting. The marketing expert will ask management whether there is branding guidance, such as a logo or colours that must be used.
  problems: The marketing expert's user requirements and competitor research were not available, so decisions were made without them. The cost of the display, and therefore whether the 12.50 euro production cost can be met, is not yet known. The cost of hypoallergenic silicone straps is still unknown. Whether to include an hourly vibration reminder is undecided, because it would cut battery life to a few months. There is still no branding guidance.
  action item SY0201b.ai1: Check the cost per unit of soft hypoallergenic silicone wrist straps. (owner D, reassigned)
  action item SY0201b.ai2: Prepare interface mock-ups showing the display layout and what the button does, for the conceptual design meeting. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0201b.ai3: Price the components, especially the display and the case. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0201b.ai4: Email the absent marketing expert today with the meeting's decisions and his tasks. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0201b.ai5: Finish the competitor research on step counters for seniors, including their screens, and send it round before the next meeting. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0201b.ai6: Send the user requirements to the team before the next meeting. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0201b.ai7: Ask management whether there is branding guidance, such as a logo or colours that must be used. (owner B, active)
  fact (absence): The marketing expert, Tom, was absent from the functional design meeting because he was ill.
  fact (plan_change): The industrial designer revised his earlier preference for a clip-on, saying that with a three-axis accelerometer the wrist is accurate enough.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer suggested a twist-off battery cover with a large coin slot, so the battery is easy to change.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed an hourly vibration reminder to move. The industrial designer said it would cut battery life to a few months, and the decision was deferred.
  fact (plan_change): The strap cost check was first assigned to the user interface designer and then reassigned to the industrial designer, who has the supplier catalogue.

[SY0201c, conceptual design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the conceptual design meeting and welcomed back the marketing expert, who confirmed he had received her email about the decisions of the previous meeting. The marketing expert presented his competitor research and user requirements: most competitors are clip-ons with small, hard-to-read screens priced between 20 and 40 euros, and seniors want readable numbers, one-handed fastening, no charging and a sense of progress. He reported that management requires the company logo to be visible on the device but leaves the colours open. The user interface designer presented her mock-ups, and the team added a ten-bar daily goal indicator with a default goal of 5,000 steps. The industrial designer priced the components at 10.80 euros per unit, including a 1.80 euro hypoallergenic silicone strap, which leaves 1.70 euros under the 12.50 euro limit before packaging. The team dropped the hourly vibration reminder and agreed on a dark grey, matte, pebble-shaped case with the logo under the display, a twist-off battery cover with a wide coin slot and a pin-and-loop strap clasp. Testing the mock-ups with seniors was offered by the user interface designer but taken on by the marketing expert, who has contacts with a seniors' walking group.
  decisions: A row of ten bars showing progress towards a daily goal will be added along the bottom of the display. The default daily goal will be 5,000 steps, set during setup by holding the button. The hourly vibration reminder is dropped. Fall detection remains parked. The battery will have a twist-off cover with a wide coin slot. The strap will use a pin-and-loop clasp rather than a buckle or a magnetic clasp. The case will be dark grey, matte and pebble-shaped, with the company logo small under the display.
  actions: The marketing expert will test the user interface designer's mock-ups with a seniors' walking group before the next meeting. The user interface designer had offered to do this. The user interface designer will send the marketing expert full-size printouts of the screens for the test. The marketing expert will send the company logo file to the industrial designer today. The industrial designer will price straps in a couple of extra colours for the next meeting. The industrial designer will make a rough clay or foam model of the device for the detailed design meeting. The user interface designer will finalise the screens, including the goal bar and the setup sequence. The project manager will write up the minutes and send them round. Someone should check the cost of packaging and the instruction leaflet, but nobody took this on.
  problems: The cost of packaging and the instruction leaflet is unknown and comes out of the same 12.50 euro budget, and nobody has taken on checking it. Whether to offer straps in several colours is undecided until extra colours have been priced. The mock-ups have not yet been tested with real seniors.
  action item SY0201c.ai1: Test the interface mock-ups with seniors (a seniors' walking group) before the next meeting. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai2: Check the cost of packaging and the instruction leaflet. (owner no owner, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai3: Send the company logo file to the industrial designer. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai4: Send the marketing expert full-size printouts of the mock-up screens for the user test. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai5: Price straps in a couple of extra colours for the next meeting. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai6: Make a rough clay or foam model of the device for the detailed design meeting. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai7: Finalise the screens, including the goal bar and the setup sequence. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0201c.ai8: Write up the minutes of the meeting and send them round. (owner A, active)
  fact (plan_change): The hourly vibration reminder, left open at the functional design meeting, has now been dropped, with the user interface designer who proposed it agreeing.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a magnetic clasp. The industrial designer said it adds about a euro and comes undone more easily.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert proposed offering straps in about three colours. The decision was deferred until extra colours are priced.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F2_TASK_TO_ABSENT [F2]: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. The gold action item owner is that absent participant.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.
- F2_REASSIGNED_OR_DROPPED [F2]: A task is assigned early in the meeting and later in the same meeting is either reassigned to someone else (status reassigned, owner = new owner, previous_owners lists the original) or dropped entirely (status dropped).
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
